title: JAGUAR URANIUM ANNOUNCES MAIDEN MINERAL RESOURCE ESTIMATE AT THE BERLIN POLYMETALLIC PROJECT IN COLOMBIA
summary: Multi-commodity mineral resource: 1.2 Mlb Indicated at 561 ppm U₃O₈ and 14.1 Mlb Inferred at 562 ppm U₃O₈. Additional critical mineral and strategic metal...
body_markdown:
- **Multi-commodity mineral resource:**


- 1.2 Mlb Indicated at 561 ppm U₃O₈ and 14.1 Mlb Inferred at 562 ppm U₃O₈.
- Additional critical mineral and strategic metal co-products, including rare earth oxides (neodymium, dysprosium, terbium and yttrium), vanadium, nickel, zinc, molybdenum and phosphate, contribute substantially to the overall contained metal value of the polymetallic deposit.


- **District-Scale** , Stratabound Carbonate-Hosted Uranium-Polymetallic Mineral Resource **encompassing the initial 2.9 km of the 10.5 km trend** .
- **Significant Expansion & Infill Potential:** The mineralized horizon remains **open along strike to the North** along the 10.5 km Berlin trend.
- **Strategic Western Supply of Critical Minerals:** Potential to provide Western Hemisphere markets with a supply of uranium, critical and strategic metals.
- **Well-Financed, Cash-Rich Balance Sheet:** Company maintains nearly US$18 million in cash and no debt
- **NSR Cut-Off Approach:** Mineral Resources are reported above a Net Smelter Return (NSR) cut-off value of US$245/t incorporating metallurgical recovery assumptions and off-site freight, smelting, and refining charges.


TORONTO


, Nov. 25, 2026


/CNW/ -- **Jaguar Uranium Corp.** (NYSE American: JAGU) (" **Jaguar** " or the " **Company** ") is pleased to announce an independent Mineral Resource Estimate (" **MRE** ") for the initial 2.9 km of the 10.5 km mineralized trend at its 100%-owned flagship Berlin Uranium-Polymetallic Project, located in Caldas Department, Colombia. The MRE was prepared in accordance with the disclosure requirements of Subpart 1300 of Regulation S-K (" **Regulation S-K 1300** ") of the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) and National Instrument 43-101 – *Standards of Disclosure for Mineral Projects* (" **NI 43-101** "). The MRE was prepared by independent geological and mining engineering consulting firm SLR International Corporation (" **SLR** "), with an effective date of November 5, 2026. All dollar values are in USD.


Continue Reading


Figure 1. Spatial Distribution of NSR-Based Mineral Resource Blocks within the Synclinal Structure: (A) and (B) illustrate the spatial distribution of mineral resource blocks estimated. The estimated resources are predominantly concentrated along the western flank and central portion of the synclinal structure. A higher density of estimated blocks is observed in the northern sector, reflecting greater drill hole coverage and sampling density. (C) and (D) provide a clearer view of the eastern flank, where significant sampling gaps and limited drill hole intersections have resulted in fewer estimated resource blocks. These areas highlight opportunities for additional drilling to improve geological continuity, increase confidence in the mineral resource estimate, and potentially expand the currently defined mineral resources.


Figure 2. Geological map of the Berlin Project showing the area covered by the current MRE and the locations of the geological cross-sections presented in Figure 4. Adjacent maps show the regional location of the project and the distribution of mineral tenements.


Figure 3. 3D views of the mineralized domains from different perspectives, distinguishing the southern sector, which comprises the 2.9 km strike length evaluated in the present MRE, and the projected continuity of the mineralized trend into the northern sector, which extends for an additional 7.6 km, defining a total mineralized trend of approximately 10.5 km.


Figure 4. Stratigraphic column of the Berlin Project. Succession C is a carbonaceous packstone unit that hosts the stratabound mineralization. Two geological cross-sections illustrate the synclinal geometry and the continuity of the mineralized horizon along both limbs of the fold and at depth.


Mineral Resources are reported above a Net Smelter Return (NSR) cut-off of US$245.00/t, an approach that incorporates metallurgical recovery assumptions as well as off-site freight, smelting and refining charges. The Mineral Resource Estimate is supported by a Reasonable Prospects for Economic Extraction (RPEE) assessment incorporating conceptual underground mining shapes.


*"This MRE marks a significant milestone for Jaguar Uranium and supports our view of Berlin as a district-scale, multi-commodity system. We have defined a uranium resource alongside a suite of critical mineral and strategic metal co-products, including rare earth oxides, vanadium, nickel, zinc, molybdenum and phosphate, across just 2.9 km of a 10.5 km trend that remains open to the north. With a strong balance sheet and no debt, we are well-funded to advance further exploration activity,"* said Steven Gold, Chief Executive Officer of Jaguar Uranium Corp.


**Mineral Resource Statement**


- SLR has prepared a MRE in accordance with Regulation S-K 1300 and CIM Definition Standards (2014). Constrained within conceptual underground stope optimization to demonstrate Reasonable Prospects for Eventual Economic Extraction (RPEE), the MRE is reported above a US$245/t Net Smelter Return (NSR) cut-off. **Classification Split:** Mineral Resources are categorized into Indicated Mineral Resources of 937 kt grading 561 ppm U3O8 (1.2 Mlb contained U3O8) and Inferred Mineral Resources of 11,343 kt grading 562 ppm U3O8 (14.1 Mlb contained U3O8), applying a bulk density of 2.72 t/m3, a long-term uranium price of US$105/lb U3O8, and 96.1% metallurgical recovery for uranium1 ( **Table 1** ).
- **Polymetallic NSR Credit Capture:** Blocks with moderate U3O8 grades (400–600 ppm) that carry high concentrations of V2O5, P2O5, rare earths (Y2O3, Nd, Dy, Tb), Ni, Zn, and Mo exceed the US$245/t NSR threshold and are captured in the resource inventory ( **Figure 1** ).


Note on Near-Surface Mineralization: The upper portion of the deposit, extending from surface to an approximate depth of 25 m and designated as the lateritized mineralized layer, was excluded from the current underground MRE, as its potential extraction would require open-pit mining methods and distinct technical and economic parameters. However, the surface expression of mineralization along both flanks represents a significant operational advantage that could facilitate future mine access and development.

**Location, Geology and Mineralization**


The Berlin Project is located in the Caldas Department, within the Central Cordillera of Colombia ( **Figure 2** ). Berlin represents a diagenetic-epigenetic mineralizing system hosted within a sedimentary succession deposited in a transitional continental-marine-lagoonal environment, which unconformably overlies the metamorphic basement of the Cajamarca Complex. Mineralization is stratabound within a permeable, carbonaceous packstone unit, ranging in thickness from 1 to 8 m, extending approximately 10.5 km along strike and exhibiting a variable lateral extent of 200 to 800 m ( **Figure 3** ). This unit served as a permeable and chemically reactive host rock, facilitating the migration of acidic, metal-bearing hydrothermal fluids and their interaction with the carbonate-rich matrix, potentially promoting metal precipitation and mineralization.


Four successions were recognized in the study area ( **Figure 4** ):


**Succession A:** Basal conglomerates interbedded with sandstones.


**Succession B:** Fossiliferous calcareous mudstones containing well-preserved bivalves and gastropods, featuring a very fine-grained texture that acted as an impermeable barrier restricting fluid mobilization.


**Succession C:** Packstone containing reworked fossil fragments, displaying wavy lamination and high concentrations of authigenic apatite and uraninite, among other minerals of interest. This succession constitutes the mineralized horizon, which varies in thickness from 1 to 8 m in the southern sector where the MRE is delineated.


**Succession D:** An upper sequence of deformed black carbonaceous shales with bioclasts, locally reaching up to 600 m in thickness, interpreted as the potential source of the mineralizing fluids.


The geological continuity of the mineralized horizon is demonstrated over several kilometers along strike, occurring as a continuous, shallowly-to-steeply dipping sedimentary layer folded into the Syncline structure ( **Figure 3** ).


**Upcoming Work Program: Extension Target & Infill Drilling**


Jaguar is currently planning a focused work program aimed at expanding the resource base and upgrading Inferred material to Indicated classification, including potential steps such as:


- **Northern Trend Extension:** Exploration drilling, trenching and surface mapping indicate that the mineralized succession remains **open along strike to the North** for an additional 7.6 km along the 10.5 km Berlin Trend ( **Figure 3** ).
- **Infill Drilling Program:** A targeted infill diamond core drilling campaign to address spatial sampling gaps identified within the current block model, improving grade continuity confidence and upgrading Inferred volumes ( **Figure 1D** ).
- **Geotechnical & Metallurgical Optimization:** Step-out sampling for flotation, leach optimization, and geotechnical domain refinement.


**Qualified Persons & Technical Reports**


The MRE was prepared under the direction of Mark Mathisen, C.P.G., Senior Principal Geologist and Yenlai Chee, C.P.G. Consulting Geologist,independent Qualified Persons from SLR International Corporation, in accordance with Regulation S-K 1300 and NI 43-101. The Qualified Persons have reviewed the historical sampling, analytical, and QA/QC data underlying the Mineral Resource estimate (MRE), together with the results of Jaguar's 2026 verification program involving the independent re-analysis of 150 archived drill core and pulp samples by SGS del Perú S.A.C., and consider the data sufficiently reliable and adequate to support the current MRE, notwithstanding limitations in historical analytical documentation and observed variability in individual assay results


Additional scientific and technical content in this news release has been reviewed and approved by Andrés Cáceres, an AIPG Certified Professional Geologist (CPG), a consultant to the Company who meets the requirements of a Qualified Person under NI 43-101 and Subpart 1300 of Regulation S-K.


A technical report prepared in accordance with NI 43-101 supporting the MRE will be filed on SEDAR+ within 45 days of this news release, and a Technical Report Summary (TRS) prepared in accordance with Regulation S-K 1300 supporting the MRE will be filed with the SEC as an exhibit to the Company's applicable SEC filing.


**About Jaguar Uranium Corp.**


Jaguar Uranium Corp. is a South America-focused uranium exploration company advancing a portfolio of prospective brownfield projects across Argentina and Colombia. In Argentina, Jaguar is advancing the Laguna Salada Project in Chubut Province and the historic Huemul uranium mine in Mendoza Province. Anchored by a former producing mine, a historic uranium district and exploration projects supported by historical drilling, the Company is focused on advancing and expanding uranium opportunities across the region. The Company's Berlin Project in Caldas Department, Colombia is a district-scale, sedimentary-hosted polymetallic system with a current MRE for uranium alongside rare earth elements, vanadium, nickel, phosphate, molybdenum and zinc. Jaguar completed a $25 million initial public offering on NYSE American in February 2026 and is led by an experienced team with backgrounds in exploration, permitting, project development and mining finance in South America.
